methodology: This is a re-classification and allowlist-design pass over F2-PREP-002's repository-evidenced edge catalogue, not a repeat full re-scan (F2-PREP-002 itself explicitly builds on, and does not duplicate, F0-004's coarser 37x37 matrix). For every one of F2-PREP-002's 124 edges + 25 direct-Prisma-access sites, this task: (a) determined whether the edge is genuinely cross-domain per this task's INVENTORY DEFINITION (owning domain of caller vs. owning domain of accessed model/service, using MODULE_MAP.md/F2-PREP-001 domain assignments) — same-domain edges mislabeled 'violation' in the source taxonomy for reasons unrelated to domain-crossing (e.g. missing $transaction within one domain's own models) were excluded, see excludedSameDomainFindings[]; (b) re-verified a representative sample per domain pair directly against current server/src source (see verificationSample[]); (c) applied the classification decision rule below to produce exactly one of the six required classifications per edge.
classificationDecisionRule: 1. Exclude edges where caller-owning-domain equals target-owning-domain (not cross-domain) or where the target is a planned/not-implemented domain or an intentionally disabled route — out of scope for this inventory.

2. If the accessed target is a real, existing, intentionally shared code contract or public HTTP boundary (a named utility/service/contract module other domains are meant to call, e.g. utils/auditLog.ts, utils/clinicScope.ts, services/fileStorage.ts, services/security/securitySignalService.ts, services/privacy/redaction.ts, the imaging bridge's token-authenticated public API, or an explicitly-blessed atomic multi-domain transaction) -> ACCEPTED_PUBLIC_CONTRACT (broadly callable) or ACCEPTED_RESTRICTED_CONTRACT (narrowly gated to one caller/transaction context).
3. Else if a repository-evidenced domain-ownership question (an F2-PREP-002 OU-* catalog item) blocks classifying who even owns the target -> UNRESOLVED_OWNERSHIP.

4. Else if the edge is a presently exploitable tenant-isolation or authorization defect (not merely a data-integrity/atomicity/concurrency defect) -> VERIFIED_SECURITY_DEFECT_REQUIRES_SEPARATE_FIX, overriding all other rules, handled per the security stop condition (not fixed here).

5. Else if source-evidenced risk is Critical or High -> PROHIBITED_NEW_PATTERN: tolerated as an existing instance so CI does not break today, but NOT blessed as accepted legacy behavior — flagged for urgent, separately-tracked remediation; no new instances of the same pattern are permitted.
6. Else (Medium/Low risk raw direct access with no formal contract) -> LEGACY_ALLOWLISTED_DIRECT_ACCESS: accepted to remain as-is for now, eligible for CI allowlisting without an urgency flag.

securityFindings.path: server/src/routes/whatsapp.ts, function getDefaultClinic() (line 1089), consumed at lines 3834/3850/3868/3883/3917/3966 by the legacy public endpoints POST /appointment-requests, POST /cancel-request, GET /services, GET /doctors, GET /availability, GET /appointment-lookup
securityFindings.exploitPreconditions: Caller must possess the single shared WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET used by authorizeWhatsappApi — the same secret value is valid for every tenant organization in the deployment, not per-organization. No other precondition (no specific target-organization knowledge is required; the vulnerable code resolves 'the' clinic as whichever one has the numerically earliest createdAt timestamp across the ENTIRE database, independent of which organization the secret nominally belongs to).
securityFindings.impact: A holder of the shared secret can create or cancel AppointmentRequest/Appointment rows, and read services/doctors/availability data, for an organization other than their own — a cross-tenant read/write, not merely a cross-tenant read.
securityFindings.recommendation: Do not fix in this evidence-only task. Recommend a dedicated, separately-authorized remediation task (proposed ID: F2-SEC-001) to replace getDefaultClinic() with real per-tenant connection resolution before this endpoint family can be considered safe to leave enabled.

securityFindings.path: server/src/routes/whatsapp.ts, Evolution WhatsApp webhook connection-resolution handler (instance-name-keyed lookup)
securityFindings.exploitPreconditions: Caller must possess the single shared WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET and know or guess a valid Evolution 'instance name' — the evidence records that this is often the clinic slug, i.e. guessable, unlike Meta/Instagram webhooks in the same file which verify a per-connection HMAC signature.
securityFindings.impact: Webhook-injection ability across every clinic using the Evolution channel — an authentication-bypass-adjacent defect, not classic tenant-isolation, but included per the stop condition because it enables cross-tenant impersonation.
securityFindings.recommendation: Do not fix in this evidence-only task. Bring Evolution webhook signature verification up to the Meta/Instagram per-connection HMAC standard, via the same recommended remediation task as SEC-01 or a follow-on.

proposedAllowlistSchema.description: A stable, structural (never line-number-based) allowlist record format a future CI enforcement task can check a diff's new/changed imports and Prisma calls against.

recordShape.callerPathGlob: string — glob matched against the changed file's repo-relative path, e.g. 'server/src/routes/whatsappInbox.ts' or 'server/src/services/privacy/**'
recordShape.ownerDomain: string — the domain code that legitimately owns the accessed target, per MODULE_MAP.md/F2-PREP-001 vocabulary; 'UNRESOLVED' or 'multiple' are valid explicit values, never silently blank
recordShape.targetModelOrSymbol: string — Prisma model name(s) and/or the exact shared-module path being accessed; never a bare line number
recordShape.accessKind: enum: read | write | delete | storage | job | import
recordShape.justificationEvidenceId: string — points at this document's edge id or the original F2-PREP-002/F2-PREP-006 id chain, so the justification is auditable rather than asserted
recordShape.expiryOrRemovalTask: string or null — the contract/candidate/task ID expected to retire this allowlist entry; null only for edges this task explicitly does not expect to ever need retiring (e.g. ACCEPTED_PUBLIC_CONTRACT entries)

proposedAllowlistSchema.enforcementIntent: A future CI rule should: (1) allow any access matching an existing allowlist record unmodified; (2) allow a matching record's callerPathGlob to gain NEW individual call sites only if the same ownerDomain/targetModelOrSymbol/accessKind tuple already exists in the allowlist (i.e. it recognizes 'more of the same accepted pattern', not a free pass for the whole file); (3) FAIL the build on any new caller-domain/owner-domain/target combination not already present in the allowlist, regardless of which classification the nearest existing entry carries; (4) treat PROHIBITED_NEW_PATTERN and VERIFIED_SECURITY_DEFECT_REQUIRES_SEPARATE_FIX entries identically to LEGACY_ALLOWLISTED_DIRECT_ACCESS for the purpose of not breaking today's build, but require CI to print a loud, non-suppressible warning banner (not just a silent pass) whenever a changed file touches one of those two classifications, naming the linked remediation task.
proposedAllowlistSchema.notCoveredByThisSchema: Same-domain transaction-integrity defects (see excludedSameDomainFindings) are out of scope for this cross-domain allowlist; a separate same-domain code-quality/lint rule would be needed for those.

classificationCounts.scopeNote: Counts cover the 66 in-scope cross-domain edges in edges[] (CDA-001..CDA-066). SEC-02 (same-domain security finding) and excludedSameDomainFindings are intentionally not counted here.

limitations: This is a re-classification of F2-PREP-002's repository-evidenced edge catalogue (baseline 70b1690c, 2026-08-02), re-verified via a targeted sample (see verificationSample[]), not a full independent re-scan of every one of the ~2,000+ prisma.<model> call sites in the codebase — the same scope caveat F2-PREP-002 itself carries forward from F0-004.

The repository has advanced from F2-PREP-002's baseline (70b1690c) to this task's baseline (6f539b23) — 40+ commits including a new inventory-unit-conversion feature. Only the edges in verificationSample[] were re-confirmed by direct source read in this pass; the remainder are carried forward from F2-PREP-002/F0-004/F2-PREP-006 evidence with a re-derived classification but without an independent re-read of every file in this task.

F2-PREP-006-A..D's full 20-candidate-command/14-candidate-query/32-characterization-test Imaging/Bridge contract catalogue was read only at the F2-PREP-006-E consolidation-summary level (via CURRENT_PHASE.md), not at the full source-document level, given this task's evidence-only, targeted-CodeGraph scope. Only the two Imaging/Bridge edges with direct, already-verified F2-PREP-002 source citations (CDA-008, CDA-048) are represented here at full depth.
Frontend (src/) cross-domain coupling is out of scope per this task's CODEGRAPH roots (backend-only). F2-PREP-002's FE-01..FE-07 are not re-carried into this inventory.

Same-domain transaction-integrity/concurrency defects (BIL-08/09/10, IMG-10, INF-12, PAT-15 and their PZ-* counterparts) are explicitly excluded from this cross-domain allowlist — see excludedSameDomainFindings[]. They remain real findings, tracked by F2-PREP-002's own top-20 remediation list, just not module-boundary edges.

The classification decision rule's risk-tier thresholds (Critical/High -> PROHIBITED_NEW_PATTERN, Medium/Low -> LEGACY_ALLOWLISTED_DIRECT_ACCESS) are this task's own synthesis, designed to satisfy the 'do not silently classify uncertain edges as accepted' instruction while staying inside the six required classification values — a later consolidation task should confirm or adjust this threshold choice explicitly rather than treat it as pre-approved.
No CI enforcement, lint rule, or dependency-cruiser configuration was implemented by this task — proposedAllowlistSchema is a design only.
nextEnforcementDependencies: External review and explicit sign-off on the classification-decision-rule (risk-tier thresholds) used in this task, since it is a synthesis not itself pre-approved by any ADR.

Consolidation with the sibling parallel-wave tasks F2-GUARDRAIL-PREP-010-B and F2-GUARDRAIL-PREP-010-C (not read by this task, per the parallel-wave isolation instruction) before any shared program-control document is updated.
Resolution of the 5 UNRESOLVED_OWNERSHIP edges (CDA-017..CDA-021 / BOD-01..BOD-04) before a boundary-lint rule can assign them a definitive owner-domain key.

A dedicated remediation task (proposed F2-SEC-001) for the VERIFIED_SECURITY_DEFECT_REQUIRES_SEPARATE_FIX finding (SEC-01, and SEC-02 if independently re-confirmed) — recommended to land BEFORE or CONCURRENTLY WITH the first CI enforcement rollout, since an allowlist that quietly tolerates a live tenant-isolation defect would undermine the guardrail's credibility.

Implementation of dependency-cruiser (or equivalent) as a report-only tool reading proposedAllowlistSchema's structural keys, scoped initially to the domains with the most PROHIBITED_NEW_PATTERN entries (clinical-appointments-availability x messaging-*, clinical-treatment-cases x inventory, core-privacy-consent-retention-dsr x multiple) before any program-wide enforcement decision.

This task's own JSON/MD pair should be superseded, not silently ignored, once F2-PREP-006's Imaging/Bridge characterization tests (32 tests) land — CDA-008 and CDA-048 should be re-verified against real test evidence at that point rather than source-read inference.
